reasoning: Per-share figures are per CURRENT pre-split share (today's Class A share plus the Class C share it gets in the Jan-2027 dividend; 8-K 2026-10-21); EV is unchanged by the dividend. Evidence, mostly primary: Q3-26 release, 10-Q and call; Q2-26 call; nine prior releases for the guidance record. The core is strong: revenue +26% (impressions +10%, price +14%), Q4 guide $73-76B (+22-27%), and Meta beat the top of its range in 6 of 8 quarters. The debate is cost: FY26 expenses $175-179B (incl. $12.3B legal), capex $135-145B, $454.5B of non-cancelable commitments ($121.4B due 2027), management 'investing aggressively' in 2027, and RL loss ~$15B. Driver build: FY27 revenue $312B (at consensus) from impressions +9% and price +10% plus new AI revenue; FoA margin 51.6% FY25 -> 37.8% FY27 -> 34.5% FY28 as D&A rises with capex that follows the AI capex file ($192B, $236B; above street). FY27 EPS ~$32 (~5% below consensus $33.9). Valuation: SOTP $750 (FoA 16.5x NTM EBIT, RL -$25B), P/E 20x $691, EV/EBITDA 10x $681 -> research target (12m) $715.83, +11% vs $642.62. Scenarios: bear $409 (25%), base $716 (50%), bull $1,019 (25%). Ladder: 75% this scenario mix (within-scenario vol 17-18%) plus 25% a market-anchored lognormal (median $650, sigma 33%, about the stock's 43% realized vol trimmed for non-earnings periods), since price is the best single forecast. That gives a median of ~$697 and P(>= $643) = 0.59. Not driver-linked: the RL venture value (-$25B), the litigation and investment adjustments, and RL revenue. Research limits: the Q3 call transcript was reached at a content_files URL; no option data was used.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led set (6 drivers: ad impressions index, price-per-ad index, FoA other revenue, FoA margin, RL loss, capex). FoA revenue = FY25 ad revenue $196,175M x impressions index x price index / 10^4 + FoA other: 98.9% of base revenue is driven, base residual 0% (198,759 reproduced exactly); RL revenue is a plain segment (1.1%), RL EBIT = -rl_loss. Value is carried by three legs on the build's own NTM figures: SOTP (w 0.45: FoA EBIT x 16.5x EV/EBIT plus RL as a stand-alone venture at -$25B, per the playbook's loss-making-venture rule), P/E 20x (w 0.35) and EV/EBITDA 10x (w 0.20) as consolidated cross-checks that include RL losses. No DCF leg (META not in dcf_policy). Leg weights are judgment, untested. Per-share values are per current pre-split share (Class C dividend effective 2027-01-19; EV unchanged).
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) the SOTP leg values RL at -$25B instead of capitalising its losses at the core multiple; that adds ~$60/share to the SOTP leg vs the P/E leg and ~+$27 to the blend (>5% judgment). (2) Capex follows the AI capex file ($192B FY27, $236B FY28), above Meta consensus ($164-186B); this lowers FY28 EBIT by ~$8-10B through D&A and raises net debt at the horizon to ~$68B. (3) The engine's FCFF does not add back SBC (~$31B in FY27), which roughly offsets net-share-settlement cash and is why the share count grows only 0.5% a year. fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value.
